 قال ابن عباس: قال النبي ﷺ: ((يرحم الله أم إسماعيل، لو تركت زمزم — أو قال: لو لم تغرف من الماء — لكانت زمزم عينًا معينًا)). قال: فشربت وأرضعت ولدها. فقال لها الملك: لا تخافوا الضيعة، فإن ها هنا بيت الله، يبني هذا الغلام وأبوه، وإن الله لا يضيع أهله. وكان البيت مرتفعًا من الأرض كالرابية، تأتيه السيول فتأخذ عن يمينه وشماله.
 فكانت كذلك حتى مرت بهم رفقة من جرهم — أو أهل بيت من جرهم — مقبلين من طريق كداء، فنزلوا في أسفل مكة، فرأوا طائرًا عائفًا، فقالوا: إن هذا الطائر ليدور على ماء، لعهدنا بهذا الوادي وما فيه ماء. فأرسلوا جريًا — أو جريين — فإذا هم بالماء. فرجعوا فأخبروهم بالماء، فأقبلوا. قال: وأم إسماعيل عند الماء. فقالوا: أتأذنين لنا أن ننزل عندك؟ فقالت: نعم، ولكن لا حق لكم في الماء. قالوا: نعم. قال ابن عباس: قال النبي ﷺ: ((فألفى ذلك أم إسماعيل، وهي تحب الإنس)). فنزلوا، وأرسلوا إلى أهليهم، فنزلوا معهم، حتى إذا كان بها أهل أبيات منهم، وشب الغلام، وتعلم العربية منهم، وأنفسهم وأعجبهم حين شب، فلما أدرك زوجوه امرأة منهم.
 وماتت أم إسماعيل، فجاء إبراهيم بعدما تزوج إسماعيل يطالع تركته، فلم يجد إسماعيل. فسأل امرأته عنه، فقالت: خرج يبتغي لنا. ثم سألها عن عيشهم وهيئتهم، فقالت: نحن بشر، نحن في ضيق وشدة، فشكت إليه. قال: فإذا جاء زوجك، فاقرئي عليه السلام، وقولي له: يغير عتبة بابه.
 فلما جاء إسماعيل، كأنه آنس شيئًا، فقال: هل جاءكم من أحد؟ قالت: نعم، جاءنا شيخ كذا وكذا، فسألنا عنك فأخبرته، وسألني كيف عيشنا، فأخبرته أنا في جهد وشدة. قال: فهل أوصاك بشيء؟ قالت: نعم، أمرني أن أقرأ عليك السلام، ويقول: غيِّر عتبة بابك. قال: ذاك أبي، وقد أمرني أن أفارقك، الحقي بأهلك. فطلقها وتزوج منهم أخرى.
 فلبث عنهم إبراهيم ما شاء الله، ثم أتاهم بعد، فلم يجده، فدخل على امرأته، فسألها عنه، فقالت: خرج يبتغي لنا. قال: كيف أنتم؟ وسألها عن عيشهم وهيئتهم، فقالت: نحن بخير وسعة، وأثنت على الله. فقال: ما طعامكم؟ قالت: اللحم. قال: فما شرابكم؟ قالت: الماء. قال: اللهم بارك لهم في اللحم والماء. قال النبي ﷺ: ((ولم يكن لهم يومئذ حب، ولو كان لهم دعا لهم فيه)). قال: فهما لا يخلو عليهما أحد بغير مكة إلا لم يوافقاه. قال: فإذا جاء زوجك، فاقرئي عليه السلام، ومريه يثبت عتبة بابه.
 فلما جاء إسماعيل قال: هل أتاكم من أحد؟ قالت: نعم، أتانا شيخ حسن الهيئة، وأثنت عليه، فسألني عنك فأخبرته، فسألني كيف عيشنا؟ فأخبرته أنا بخير. قال: فأوصاك بشيء؟ قالت: نعم، هو يقرأ عليك السلام، ويأمرك أن تثبت عتبة بابك. قال: ذاك أبي، وأنت العتبة، أمرني أن أمسكك.
 ثم لبث عنهم ما شاء الله، ثم جاء بعد ذلك، وإسماعيل يبري نبلًا له تحت دوحة قريبًا من زمزم. فلما رآه قام إليه، فصنعا كما يصنع الوالد بالولد والولد بالوالد. ثم قال: يا إسماعيل، إن الله أمرني بأمر. قال: فاصنع ما أمرك ربك. قال: وتعينني؟ قال: وأعينك. قال: فإن الله أمرني أن أبني ها هنا بيتًا — وأشار إلى أكمة مرتفعة على ما حولها. قال: فعند ذلك رفعا القواعد من البيت، فجعل إسماعيل يأتي بالحجارة، وإبراهيم يبني، حتى إذا ارتفع البناء، جاء بهذا الحجر فوضعه له، فقام عليه وهو يبني، وإسماعيل يناوله الحجارة، وهما يقولان: (رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) [البقرة: ١٢٧]. قال: فجعلا يبنيان حتى يدورا حول البيت، وهما يقولان: (رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٦٤).
8396 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The first time women took a waist-belt was because of the mother of Isma‘il. She took a waist-belt to conceal her tracks from Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Isma‘il, while she was nursing him, until he placed them by the House, near a large tree above Zamzam in the upper part of the Mosque. At that time there was no one in Makkah, and there was no water there. He placed them there and placed with them a bag containing dates and a water-skin containing water. Then Ibrahim turned away, leaving. The mother of Isma‘il followed him and said: “O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there are no people and nothing?” She said that to him repeatedly, but he did not turn toward her. She said to him: “Is it Allah who commanded you to do this?” He said: “Yes.” She said: “Then He will not abandon us.” Then she returned, and Ibrahim went on until he reached the mountain pass where they could not see him. He faced the House, raised his hands, and supplicated with these words: “Our Lord, indeed I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation…” until he reached: “that they may be grateful” [Ibrahim: 37].
 The mother of Isma‘il continued nursing Isma‘il and drinking from that water until what was in the water-skin ran out. She became thirsty, and her son became thirsty. She began looking at him twisting — or he said: thrashing — so she went away, disliking to look at him. She found that al-Ṣafa was the nearest mountain to her on the earth, so she stood upon it. Then she faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. She descended from al-Ṣafa until, when she reached the valley, she raised the edge of her garment and then ran with the running of a person in distress until she crossed the valley. Then she came to al-Marwah, stood upon it, and looked to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. She did that seven times. Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “That is why the people perform sa‘y between them.”
 When she overlooked al-Marwah, she heard a voice. She said: “Quiet!” — meaning herself — then listened and heard it again. She said: “You have made yourself heard; if you have any help, then help.” Behold, there was the angel at the place of Zamzam. He dug with his heel — or he said: with his wing — until the water appeared. She began making a basin around it, saying with her hand like this, and she began scooping water into her water-skin while it continued to gush after she scooped.
 Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma‘il. Had she left Zamzam — or he said: had she not scooped from the water — Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.” He said: She drank and nursed her child. The angel said to her: “Do not fear being abandoned, for here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build. Allah does not abandon His people.” The House was raised above the earth like a hillock; floods would come and pass to its right and left.
 She remained like that until a group from Jurhum — or a household from Jurhum — passed by them, coming from the direction of Kada’. They descended at the lower part of Makkah and saw a bird circling. They said: “This bird is surely circling over water, and we know this valley well, and there is no water in it.” They sent one or two scouts, and behold, there was water. They returned and informed them about the water, so they came forward. He said: The mother of Isma‘il was at the water. They said: “Do you permit us to settle near you?” She said: “Yes, but you have no right to the water.” They said: “Yes.” Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “That suited the mother of Isma‘il, for she loved human company.” They settled there and sent for their families, who settled with them, until there were households from them there. The boy grew up and learned Arabic from them. They loved him dearly and admired him when he grew up. When he reached maturity, they married him to a woman from among them.
 The mother of Isma‘il died, and Ibrahim came after Isma‘il had married, checking on the family he had left. He did not find Isma‘il, so he asked his wife about him. She said: “He has gone out seeking provision for us.” Then he asked her about their livelihood and condition, and she said: “We are in hardship. We are in narrowness and difficulty,” and she complained to him. He said: “When your husband comes, convey salām to him and tell him to change the threshold of his door.”
 When Isma‘il came, he sensed something and said: “Did anyone come to you?” She said: “Yes, an old man of such-and-such description came to us. He asked us about you, so I informed him. He asked me how our life was, so I informed him that we are in hardship and difficulty.” He said: “Did he advise you with anything?” She said: “Yes, he commanded me to convey salām to you, and he says: Change the threshold of your door.” He said: “That was my father, and he has commanded me to separate from you. Go back to your family.” So he divorced her and married another woman from among them.
 Ibrahim remained away from them as long as Allah willed, then came to them afterward but did not find him. He entered upon his wife and asked her about him. She said: “He has gone out seeking provision for us.” He said: “How are you?” He asked her about their livelihood and condition. She said: “We are in goodness and ease,” and she praised Allah. He said: “What is your food?” She said: “Meat.” He said: “What is your drink?” She said: “Water.” He said: “O Allah, bless them in meat and water.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “They had no grain that day; had they had it, he would have supplicated for them regarding it.” He said: No one consumes them both outside Makkah except that they do not agree with him. He said: “When your husband comes, convey salām to him and command him to keep firm the threshold of his door.”
 When Isma‘il came, he said: “Did anyone come to you?” She said: “Yes, a handsome old man came to us,” and she praised him. “He asked me about you, so I informed him. He asked me how our life was, so I informed him that we are well.” He said: “Did he advise you with anything?” She said: “Yes, he conveys salām to you and commands you to keep firm the threshold of your door.” He said: “That was my father, and you are the threshold. He commanded me to keep you.”
 Then he remained away from them as long as Allah willed, and then came afterward while Isma‘il was sharpening arrows of his beneath a large tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he rose to him, and they did as a father does with his son and as a son does with his father. Then he said: “O Isma‘il, Allah has commanded me with a matter.” He said: “Do what your Lord commanded you.” He said: “Will you help me?” He said: “I will help you.” He said: “Allah has commanded me to build a House here,” and he pointed to a raised mound above what surrounded it. He said: At that point they raised the foundations of the House. Isma‘il would bring the stones, and Ibrahim would build. When the building became high, he brought this stone and placed it for him; he stood upon it while building, and Isma‘il handed him the stones. They were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing” [al-Baqarah: 127]. He said: They kept building until they went around the House, while saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3364).

 ثم لبث عنهم ما شاء الله، ثم جاء بعد ذلك، وإسماعيل يبري نبلًا له تحت دوحة قريبًا من زمزم. فلما رآه قام إليه، فصنعا كما يصنع الوالد بالولد والولد بالوالد. ثم قال: يا إسماعيل، إن الله أمرني بأمر. قال: فاصنع ما أمرك ربك. قال: وتعينني؟ قال: وأعينك. قال: فإن الله أمرني أن أبني ها هنا بيتًا — وأشار إلى أكمة مرتفعة على ما حولها. قال: فعند ذلك رفعا القواعد من البيت، فجعل إسماعيل يأتي بالحجارة، وإبراهيم يبني، حتى إذا ارتفع البناء، جاء بهذا الحجر فوضعه له، فقام عليه وهو يبني، وإسماعيل يناوله الحجارة، وهما يقولان: (رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) [البقرة: ١٢٧]. قال: فجعلا يبنيان حتى يدورا حول البيت، وهما يقولان: (رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٦٤).
8396 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The first time women took a waist-belt was because of the mother of Isma‘il. She took a waist-belt to conceal her tracks from Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Isma‘il, while she was nursing him, until he placed them by the House, near a large tree above Zamzam in the upper part of the Mosque. At that time there was no one in Makkah, and there was no water there. He placed them there and placed with them a bag containing dates and a water-skin containing water. Then Ibrahim turned away, leaving. The mother of Isma‘il followed him and said: “O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there are no people and nothing?” She said that to him repeatedly, but he did not turn toward her. She said to him: “Is it Allah who commanded you to do this?” He said: “Yes.” She said: “Then He will not abandon us.” Then she returned, and Ibrahim went on until he reached the mountain pass where they could not see him. He faced the House, raised his hands, and supplicated with these words: “Our Lord, indeed I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation…” until he reached: “that they may be grateful” [Ibrahim: 37].
 The mother of Isma‘il continued nursing Isma‘il and drinking from that water until what was in the water-skin ran out. She became thirsty, and her son became thirsty. She began looking at him twisting — or he said: thrashing — so she went away, disliking to look at him. She found that al-Ṣafa was the nearest mountain to her on the earth, so she stood upon it. Then she faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. She descended from al-Ṣafa until, when she reached the valley, she raised the edge of her garment and then ran with the running of a person in distress until she crossed the valley. Then she came to al-Marwah, stood upon it, and looked to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. She did that seven times. Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “That is why the people perform sa‘y between them.”
 When she overlooked al-Marwah, she heard a voice. She said: “Quiet!” — meaning herself — then listened and heard it again. She said: “You have made yourself heard; if you have any help, then help.” Behold, there was the angel at the place of Zamzam. He dug with his heel — or he said: with his wing — until the water appeared. She began making a basin around it, saying with her hand like this, and she began scooping water into her water-skin while it continued to gush after she scooped.
 Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma‘il. Had she left Zamzam — or he said: had she not scooped from the water — Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.” He said: She drank and nursed her child. The angel said to her: “Do not fear being abandoned, for here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build. Allah does not abandon His people.” The House was raised above the earth like a hillock; floods would come and pass to its right and left.
 She remained like that until a group from Jurhum — or a household from Jurhum — passed by them, coming from the direction of Kada’. They descended at the lower part of Makkah and saw a bird circling. They said: “This bird is surely circling over water, and we know this valley well, and there is no water in it.” They sent one or two scouts, and behold, there was water. They returned and informed them about the water, so they came forward. He said: The mother of Isma‘il was at the water. They said: “Do you permit us to settle near you?” She said: “Yes, but you have no right to the water.” They said: “Yes.” Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “That suited the mother of Isma‘il, for she loved human company.” They settled there and sent for their families, who settled with them, until there were households from them there. The boy grew up and learned Arabic from them. They loved him dearly and admired him when he grew up. When he reached maturity, they married him to a woman from among them.
 The mother of Isma‘il died, and Ibrahim came after Isma‘il had married, checking on the family he had left. He did not find Isma‘il, so he asked his wife about him. She said: “He has gone out seeking provision for us.” Then he asked her about their livelihood and condition, and she said: “We are in hardship. We are in narrowness and difficulty,” and she complained to him. He said: “When your husband comes, convey salām to him and tell him to change the threshold of his door.”
 When Isma‘il came, he sensed something and said: “Did anyone come to you?” She said: “Yes, an old man of such-and-such description came to us. He asked us about you, so I informed him. He asked me how our life was, so I informed him that we are in hardship and difficulty.” He said: “Did he advise you with anything?” She said: “Yes, he commanded me to convey salām to you, and he says: Change the threshold of your door.” He said: “That was my father, and he has commanded me to separate from you. Go back to your family.” So he divorced her and married another woman from among them.
 Ibrahim remained away from them as long as Allah willed, then came to them afterward but did not find him. He entered upon his wife and asked her about him. She said: “He has gone out seeking provision for us.” He said: “How are you?” He asked her about their livelihood and condition. She said: “We are in goodness and ease,” and she praised Allah. He said: “What is your food?” She said: “Meat.” He said: “What is your drink?” She said: “Water.” He said: “O Allah, bless them in meat and water.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “They had no grain that day; had they had it, he would have supplicated for them regarding it.” He said: No one consumes them both outside Makkah except that they do not agree with him. He said: “When your husband comes, convey salām to him and command him to keep firm the threshold of his door.”
 When Isma‘il came, he said: “Did anyone come to you?” She said: “Yes, a handsome old man came to us,” and she praised him. “He asked me about you, so I informed him. He asked me how our life was, so I informed him that we are well.” He said: “Did he advise you with anything?” She said: “Yes, he conveys salām to you and commands you to keep firm the threshold of your door.” He said: “That was my father, and you are the threshold. He commanded me to keep you.”
 Then he remained away from them as long as Allah willed, and then came afterward while Isma‘il was sharpening arrows of his beneath a large tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he rose to him, and they did as a father does with his son and as a son does with his father. Then he said: “O Isma‘il, Allah has commanded me with a matter.” He said: “Do what your Lord commanded you.” He said: “Will you help me?” He said: “I will help you.” He said: “Allah has commanded me to build a House here,” and he pointed to a raised mound above what surrounded it. He said: At that point they raised the foundations of the House. Isma‘il would bring the stones, and Ibrahim would build. When the building became high, he brought this stone and placed it for him; he stood upon it while building, and Isma‘il handed him the stones. They were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing” [al-Baqarah: 127]. He said: They kept building until they went around the House, while saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3364).

٨٣٩٧ — عن علي بن أبي طالب مرفوعًا: ((أول من فتق الله لسانه بالعربية المبينة إسماعيل)).
 حسن: رواه الزبير بن بكار في النسب. قاله الحافظ ابن حجر في الفتح (٦/٤٠٣).
 وقوله: “أول من فتق لسانه بالعربية” أي أول من تكلم بالعربية في الحجاز وما حولها؛ لأن العربية هي لغة أهل اليمن، وتعلم إسماعيل عليه السلام منهم عندما نزلوا في مكة حول زمزم، كما جاء في كلام ابن عباس في صحيح البخاري (٣٣٦٤).

english_source:
8397 — ‘Ali ibn Abi Ṭalib narrated in marfu‘ form: “The first whose tongue Allah opened with clear Arabic was Isma‘il.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in al-Nasab. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar stated this in al-Fatḥ (6/403).
 His saying, “the first whose tongue was opened with Arabic,” means the first to speak Arabic in the Hijaz and its surrounding areas, because Arabic was the language of the people of Yemen, and Isma‘il, peace be upon him, learned it from them when they settled in Makkah around Zamzam, as appears in the statement of Ibn ‘Abbas in Ṣaḥiḥ al-Bukhari (3364).

٨٣٩٨ — عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: مر النبي ﷺ على نفر من أسلم ينتضلون، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ارموا بني إسماعيل، فإن أباكم كان راميًا، ارموا وأنا مع بني فلان)). قال: فأمسك أحد الفريقين بأيديهم، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ما لكم لا ترمون؟)) فقالوا: يا رسول الله، نرمي وأنت معهم؟ قال: ((ارموا، وأنا معكم كلكم)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٧٣).

8398 — Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a group from Aslam who were competing in archery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Shoot, O children of Isma‘il, for your father was an archer. Shoot, and I am with the sons of so-and-so.” He said: One of the two groups held back their hands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What is wrong with you that you are not shooting?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, should we shoot while you are with them?” He said: “Shoot, for I am with all of you.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3373).

٨٣٩٩ — عن أبي هريرة قال: خرج رسول الله ﷺ وأسلم يرمون، فقال: ((ارموا بني إسماعيل؛ فإن أباكم كان راميًا، وارموا وأنا مع ابن الأدرع)). فأمسك القوم قسيّهم، وقالوا: من كنت معه غلب. قال: ((ارموا، وأنا معكم كلكم)).
 حسن: رواه أبو يعلى (٦١١٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٦٩٥)، والحاكم (٢/٩٤).

8399 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out while Aslam were shooting arrows. He said: “Shoot, O children of Isma‘il, for your father was an archer. Shoot, and I am with Ibn al-Adra‘.” The people held back their bows and said: “Whoever you are with will win.” He said: “Shoot, for I am with all of you.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Ya‘la (6119), and Ibn Hibban (4695) and al-Hakim (2/94) authenticated it.

Shoot, and I am with Ibn al-Adra‘.” The people held back their bows and said: “Whoever you are with will win.” He said: “Shoot, for I am with all of you.”

8400 — Abu al-Ṭufayl said: I said to Ibn ‘Abbas: “Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed sa‘y between al-Ṣafa and al-Marwah, and that this is a Sunnah.” He said: “They have spoken the truth. When Ibrahim was commanded with the rites, Satan appeared to him at the place of sa‘y, so he raced him, and Ibrahim outran him. Then Jibril took him to Jamrat al-‘Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him — Yunus said: ‘the Satan’ — so he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then he appeared to him at the middle jamrah, and he threw seven pebbles at him.” He said: “He had laid him down upon his forehead” — Yunus said: “And there he laid him down upon his forehead” — “and Isma‘il was wearing a white shirt. He said: ‘My father, I have no garment in which you can shroud me except this, so remove it so you may shroud me in it.’ He began trying to remove it, and he was called from behind: ‘O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision.’ Ibrahim turned, and behold, there was a white ram, horned and with large eyes.”
 Ibn ‘Abbas said: “I remember us selling this kind of ram.” He said: Then Jibril took him to the farthest jamrah, and Satan appeared to him, so he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then Jibril took him to Mina and said: “This is Mina.” Then he mentioned the hadith at length.
 Good: Narrated by Ahmad (2707), Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (2820), and Abu Dawud (1885).

٨٤٠٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سئل رسول الله ﷺ: من أكرم الناس؟ قال: ((أتقاهم لله)). قالوا: ليس عن هذا نسألك. قال: ((فأكرم الناس يوسف نبي الله، ابن نبي الله، ابن نبي الله، ابن خليل الله)). قالوا: ليس عن هذا نسألك. قال: ((فعن معادن العرب تسألوني؟ الناس معادن، خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٨٣)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٩).

8402 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: “Who are the most noble of people?” He said: “Those most mindful of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Close Friend of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Are you asking me about the origins of the Arabs? People are like mines; the best of them in the Age of Ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3383) and Muslim (2379).

٨٤٠٣ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((نحن أحق بالشك من إبراهيم إذ قال: (رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ، قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن؟ قَالَ بَلَىٰ، وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي)، ويرحم الله لوطًا، لقد كان يأوي إلى ركن شديد، ولو لبثت في السجن طول ما لبث يوسف لأجبت الداعي)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٧٢)، ومسلم (١٥١: ٢٣٨).
 ومعنى قوله: “لأجبت الداعي” هو رسول الملك الوارد ذكره في الآية:
 (فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ، قَالَ: ارْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ، فَاسْأَلْهُ مَا بَالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ، إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ) [يوسف: ٥٠].

8403 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We have more right to doubt than Ibrahim when he said: ‘My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.’ He said: ‘Have you not believed?’ He said: ‘Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured.’ May Allah have mercy on Luṭ; he truly used to take refuge in a strong support. And if I had remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, I would have answered the caller.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3372) and Muslim (151:238).
 The meaning of his saying “I would have answered the caller” is the messenger of the king mentioned in the verse:
 “When the messenger came to him, he said: Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot.” [Yusuf: 50]
 His saying, “We have more right to doubt than Ibrahim,” is intended to negate doubt from Ibrahim and affirm his strong faith, by attributing doubt to himself — and doubt is certainly negated from him ﷺ. What is meant by “support” is a clan and a group. The Prophet ﷺ showed mercy toward his in-law at the time when his chest tightened and his distress became severe because of what his people had brought upon him, until he said: “or could take refuge in a strong support,” meaning a clan. Yet he should have taken refuge in the strongest support, which is Allah, Glorified and Most High. It is possible that he forgot that, then remembered and turned to Allah, Glorified and Most High.

8404 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: “Who are the most noble of people?” He said: “Those most mindful of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Close Friend of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Are you asking me about the origins of the Arabs? People are like mines; the best of them in the Age of Ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3383) and Muslim (2379).

٨٤٠٦ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ — في حديثها عن الإفك — قال النبي ﷺ: ((إن كنت بريئة فسيبرئك الله، وإن كنت ألممت بذنب فاستغفري الله وتوبي إليه)). قلت: إني والله لا أجد مثلًا إلا أبا يوسف: (وَجَاءُوا عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ. قَالَ: بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا، فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ، وَاللهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ) [يوسف: ١٨]. وأنزل الله: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِّنكُمْ، لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَّكُم، بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ، لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِّنْهُم مَّا اكْتَسَبَ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ، وَالَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبْرَهُ مِنْهُمْ لَهُ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ) [النور: ١١] العشر الآيات.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٦٩٠)، ومسلم (٢٧٧٠: ٥٦).
وذكر أهل الكتاب: لما مات يعقوب بكى عليه أهل مصر سبعين يومًا، وأمر يوسف الأطباء فطيّبوه بعليب، ومكث فيه أربعين يومًا، ثم استأذن يوسف ملك مصر في الخروج مع أبيه ليدفنه عند أهله، فأذن له. فخرج معه أكابر مصر وشيوخها، فلما وصلوا حبرون دفنوه في المغارة التي كان اشتراها إبراهيم الخليل من عفرون بن صخر الحثي، فدفنوه فيها، وعملوا له عزاء سبعة أيام، ثم رجعوا إلى مصر. هكذا ذكره ابن جرير في تاريخه، وابن كثير في البداية والنهاية (١/٥٠٤)، وهو في سفر التكوين (٤٩: ٢٦-٣٣).
 وكان عمر يعقوب يوم دخل مصر مائة وثلاثين سنة، وأقام بأرض مصر سبع عشرة سنة، فكان عمره عند وفاته مائة وسبعًا وأربعين سنة.

8406 — ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ — in her hadith about the false accusation — narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence; and if you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.” I said: “By Allah, I do not find an example except the father of Yusuf: ‘And they came with false blood upon his shirt. He said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is beautiful, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe’ [Yusuf: 18].” Then Allah revealed: “Indeed, those who came with the false accusation are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he earned of sin, and the one who took upon himself the greater portion of it will have a great punishment” [al-Nur: 11], the ten verses.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4690) and Muslim (2770:56).
The People of the Book mentioned: When Ya‘qub died, the people of Egypt wept over him for seventy days. Yusuf ordered the physicians, so they embalmed him with aloe, and he remained in it for forty days. Then Yusuf asked permission from the king of Egypt to leave with his father in order to bury him with his family, and he permitted him. The elders and chiefs of Egypt went out with him. When they reached Hebron, they buried him in the cave that Ibrahim, the Close Friend, had purchased from Ephron ibn Ṣakhar the Hittite. They buried him there and held mourning for him for seven days, then returned to Egypt. This is how Ibn Jarir mentioned it in his History, and Ibn Kathir in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (1/504), and it is in the Book of Genesis (49:26–33).
 Ya‘qub’s age when he entered Egypt was one hundred and thirty years. He stayed in the land of Egypt for seventeen years, so his age at the time of his death was one hundred and forty-seven years.

٨٤٠٧ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سئل رسول الله ﷺ: من أكرم الناس؟ قال: ((أتقاهم لله)). قالوا: ليس عن هذا نسألك. قال: ((فأكرم الناس يوسف نبي الله، ابن نبي الله، ابن نبي الله، ابن خليل الله)). قالوا: ليس عن هذا نسألك. قال: ((فعن معادن العرب تسألوني؟ الناس معادن، خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٨٣)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٩).

8407 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: “Who are the most noble of people?” He said: “Those most mindful of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Close Friend of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Are you asking me about the origins of the Arabs? People are like mines; the best of them in the Age of Ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3383) and Muslim (2379).

8407 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: “Who are the most noble of people?” He said: “Those most mindful of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Close Friend of Allah.” They said: “We are not asking you about this.” He said: “Are you asking me about the origins of the Arabs? People are like mines; the best of them in the Age of Ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3383) and Muslim (2379).

arabic_source:
٨٤٠٨ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: مرض النبي ﷺ، فاشتد مرضه، فقال: ((مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس)). قالت عائشة: إنه رجل رقيق، إذا قام مقامك لم يستطع أن يصلي بالناس. قال: ((مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس)). فعادت، فقال: ((مري أبا بكر فليصل بالناس، فإنكن صواحب يوسف)). فأتاه الرسول، فصلى بالناس في حياة النبي ﷺ.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٧٨)، ومسلم (٤٢٠: ١٠١).

8408 — Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari said: The Prophet ﷺ became ill, and his illness became severe. He said: “Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “He is a soft-hearted man; when he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He said: “Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” She repeated herself, so he said: “Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer, for you are the women around Yusuf.” The messenger came to him, and he led the people in prayer during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (678) and Muslim (420:101).

٨٤٠٩ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: لما اشتد برسول الله ﷺ وجعه، قيل له في الصلاة، فقال: ((مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس)). قالت عائشة: إن أبا بكر رجل رقيق، إذا قرأ غلبه البكاء. قال: ((مروه فليصل)). فعاودته، قال: ((مروه فليصل، إنكن صواحب يوسف)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٨٢).

8409 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: When the pain of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became severe, the matter of prayer was mentioned to him. He said: “Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “Abu Bakr is a soft-hearted man; when he recites, weeping overcomes him.” He said: “Command him to lead the prayer.” She repeated herself, and he said: “Command him to lead the prayer; you are the women around Yusuf.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (682).

٨٤١٠ — عن عائشة أن النبي ﷺ قال لها: ((مري أبا بكر يصلي بالناس)). قالت: إنه رجل أسيف، متى يقم مقامك رق. فعاد، فعادت. قال شعبة: فقال في الثالثة أو الرابعة: ((إنكن صواحب يوسف، مروا أبا بكر)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٨٤)، ومسلم (٤١٨: ٩٤).

8410 — ‘A’ishah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to her: “Command Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” She said: “He is a sorrowful man; whenever he stands in your place, he becomes overcome with emotion.” He repeated it, and she repeated her concern. Shu‘bah said: On the third or fourth time, he said: “You are the women around Yusuf. Command Abu Bakr.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3384) and Muslim (418:94).

٨٤١١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((اللهم أنج عياش بن أبي ربيعة، اللهم أنج سلمة بن هشام، اللهم أنج الوليد بن الوليد، اللهم أنج المستضعفين من المؤمنين، اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر، اللهم اجعلها سنين كسني يوسف)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٨٦).

english_source:
8411 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, save ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah. O Allah, save Salamah ibn Hisham. O Allah, save al-Walid ibn al-Walid. O Allah, save the oppressed believers. O Allah, intensify Your grip upon Muḍar. O Allah, make them years like the years of Yusuf.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3386).

٨٤١٢ — عن مالك بن صعصعة قال: قال النبي ﷺ: ((بينا أنا عند البيت بين النائم واليقظان…)) فذكر حديث المعراج، وفيه: ((فأتينا السماء الثالثة، قيل: من هذا؟ قيل: جبريل. قيل: من معك؟ قيل: محمد. قيل: وقد أرسل إليه؟ قال: نعم. قيل: مرحبًا به، ولنعم المجيء جاء. فأتيت على يوسف، فسلمت عليه. قال: مرحبًا بك من أخ ونبي)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢٠٧)، ومسلم (١٦٤: ٢٦٤).

8412 — Malik ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “While I was at the House, between sleep and wakefulness…” He mentioned the hadith of the Mi‘raj, and in it occurs: “Then we came to the third heaven. It was said: Who is this? It was said: Jibril. It was said: Who is with you? It was said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, and what an excellent arrival he has made. Then I came upon Yusuf and greeted him with salām. He said: Welcome to you as a brother and a prophet.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3207) and Muslim (164:264).

٨٤١٣ — عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((أُتيت بالبراق…)) حديث الإسراء، وفيه: ((فإذا أنا بيوسف ﷺ، إذا هو قد أُعطي شطر الحسن، فرحب ودعا لي بخير)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٢: ٢٥٩).
 وقوله: “أُعطي شطر الحسن” أي على النصف من حسن أبينا آدم عليه السلام؛ لأن الله تعالى خلق آدم بيده، ونفخ فيه من روحه، فكان في غاية نهايات الحسن البشري، ولذا يدخل أهل الجنة الجنة على طول أبيهم آدم وصورته وحسنه، كما ورد ذلك في حديث أبي هريرة عند البخاري في أحاديث الأنبياء (٣٣٢٧)، ومسلم في صفة الجنة (٢٨٣٤: ١٥، ١٦). إلا أن هذا الحسن كان فيما بين آدم وبين يوسف عليهما السلام، وإلا فنبينا ﷺ كان من أجل الناس وأحسنهم مطلقًا منذ آدم إلى يوم القيامة.

8413 — Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was brought al-Buraq…” the hadith of the Isra’, and in it occurs: “Then there I was with Yusuf ﷺ, and he had been given half of beauty. He welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (162:259).
 His saying, “He was given half of beauty,” means half of the beauty of our father Adam, peace be upon him, because Allah Most High created Adam with His hand and breathed into him of His spirit, so he was at the highest limit of human beauty. For this reason, the people of Paradise will enter Paradise upon the height, form, and beauty of their father Adam, as reported in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in al-Bukhari in the Book of the Prophets (3327), and Muslim in the Description of Paradise (2834:15,16). However, this beauty refers to what was between Adam and Yusuf, peace be upon them both; otherwise, our Prophet ﷺ was absolutely the most majestic and beautiful of people from Adam until the Day of Resurrection.

٨٤١٤ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((بينما أيوب يغتسل عريانًا، خر عليه رِجل جراد من ذهب، فجعل يحثي في ثوبه، فناداه ربه: يا أيوب، ألم أكن أغنيتك عما ترى؟ قال: بلى يا رب، ولكن لا غنى لي عن بركتك)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٩١) و(٧٤٩٣).

8414 — Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “While Ayyub was bathing naked, a swarm of golden locusts fell upon him. He began scooping them into his garment. His Lord called to him: O Ayyub, had I not made you free of need from what you see? He said: Yes, my Lord, but I cannot do without Your blessing.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3391) and (7493).

arabic_source:
٨٤١٥ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((لما عافى الله أيوب أمطر عليه جرادًا من ذهب، فجعل يأخذه بيده ويجعله في ثوبه، فقيل له: يا أيوب، أما تشبع؟ قال: ومن يشبع من رحمتك؟)).
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (٢٥٧٧)، وأحمد (١٠٦٣٨)، وابن حبان (٦٢٣٠)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٢٥٣٣)، والحاكم (٢/٥٨٢) — واللفظ له —، كلهم من طرق همام، عن قتادة، عن النضر بن أنس، عن بشير بن نهيك، عن أبي هريرة. وقال الحاكم: «هذا حديث صحيح على شرط البخاري ولم يخرجاه».
وقد ابتلي أيوب بلاء فصبر واحتسب حتى ضُرب المثل بصبره، حتى فرج الله عنه وعظم له الأجر.
ورُوي عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((إن أيوب نبي الله ﷺ لبث في بلائه ثمان عشرة سنة، فرفضه القريب والبعيد إلا رجلين من إخوانه كانا من أخص إخوانه، كانا يغدوان إليه ويروحان. فقال أحدهما لصاحبه: تعلم والله لقد أذنب أيوب ذنبًا ما أذنبه أحد من العالمين. قال له صاحبه: وما ذاك؟ قال: منذ ثمان عشرة سنة لم يرحمه الله فيكشف ما به. فلما راح إليه لم يصبر الرجل حتى ذكر ذلك له، فقال أيوب: لا أدري ما تقول، غير أن الله يعلم أني كنت أمر على الرجلين يتنازعان فيذكران الله، فأرجع إلى بيتي فأكفر عنهما كراهية أن يذكر الله إلا في حق...)) إلى آخر الحديث.
رواه الطبري في تفسيره (٢٠/١٠٩)، والبزار — الكشف (٢٣٥٧) —، وابن حبان (٢٨٩٨) — واللفظ له —، والحاكم (٢/٥٨١-٥٨٢)، كلهم من طريق نافع بن يزيد، عن عقيل، عن ابن شهاب، عن أنس بن مالك.
قال الحاكم: صحيح على شرط الشيخين ولم يخرجاه. وقال البزار: لا نعلم رواه عن الزهري عن أنس إلا عقيل، ولا عنه إلا نافع، ورواه عن نافع غير واحد.
قلت: نافع بن يزيد مع تفرده بذلك خولف أيضًا؛ فقد خالفه يونس بن يزيد الأيلي، فرواه عن عقيل، عن ابن شهاب، عن النبي ﷺ مرسلًا، ولم يذكر فيه أنسًا. أخرج حديثه الطحاوي في شرح المشكل (٤٥٩٦) عن إبراهيم بن أبي داود، حدثنا نعيم بن حماد، حدثنا ابن المبارك، عن يونس بن يزيد.
وهذا أولى من رواية نافع بن يزيد؛ فإن رواية يونس من طريق ابن المبارك عنه أقوى.
وقال ابن كثير في البداية والنهاية (١/٥١١): «وهذا غريب رفعه جدًا، والأشبه أن يكون موقوفًا». وقال الطبري في تاريخه (١/٣٢٤-٣٢٥): «لما توفي أيوب كان عمره ثلاثًا وتسعين سنة».

8415 — Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “When Allah cured Ayyub, He rained golden locusts upon him. He began taking them with his hand and placing them in his garment. It was said to him: O Ayyub, are you not satisfied? He said: Who can ever be satisfied with Your mercy?”
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (2577), Ahmad (10638), Ibn Hibban (6230), al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (2533), and al-Hakim (2/582), whose wording this is, all through routes from Hammam, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah. Al-Hakim said: “This hadith is authentic according to the condition of al-Bukhari, though they did not narrate it.”
Ayyub was tested with severe affliction, and he remained patient and sought reward, until his patience became proverbial; then Allah relieved him and magnified his reward.
It is also reported from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that Ayyub, the Prophet of Allah, remained in his affliction for eighteen years, and that those near and far abandoned him except two of his closest brothers who used to visit him morning and evening. One of them said that Ayyub must have committed a sin unlike anyone else because Allah had not relieved him for eighteen years. When this was mentioned to Ayyub, he said that he did not know what the man meant, except that Allah knew that whenever he passed two men disputing and mentioning Allah, he would return home and offer expiation on their behalf out of dislike that Allah be mentioned except in truth. The report continues at length.
Al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (20/109), al-Bazzar — al-Kashf (2357) —, Ibn Hibban (2898), whose wording this is, and al-Hakim (2/581–582), all through Nafi‘ ibn Yazid, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik.
Al-Hakim declared it authentic according to the condition of the two Shaykhs. Al-Bazzar said that he knew no one to narrate it from al-Zuhri from Anas except ‘Uqayl, nor from ‘Uqayl except Nafi‘, though more than one narrated it from Nafi‘.
I say: Nafi‘ ibn Yazid, despite being alone in this route, was also contradicted by Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli, who narrated it from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from the Prophet ﷺ in mursal form without mentioning Anas. Al-Tahawi narrated that route in Sharh al-Mushkil (4596) through Ibrahim ibn Abi Dawud, from Nu‘aym ibn Hammad, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Yunus ibn Yazid.
This route is preferable to the narration of Nafi‘ ibn Yazid, because Yunus’s narration through Ibn al-Mubarak is stronger.
Ibn Kathir said in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (1/511): “Its being raised to the Prophet is extremely strange; it is more likely to be mawquf.” Al-Tabari said in his History (1/324–325): “When Ayyub died, he was ninety-three years old.”

٨٤٢١ — عن عبد الله بن جعفر قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((ما ينبغي لنبي أن يقول: إني خير من يونس بن متى)).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٦٧٠)، وأحمد (١٧٥٧)، وأبو يعلى (٦٧٩٣).
 قلت: يُحمل قول النبي ﷺ على تواضع منه، وإلا فقد قال الله تعالى: (تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ، مِّنْهُم مَّن كَلَّمَ اللهُ، وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ) [البقرة: ٢٥٣].
 وقال النبي ﷺ: ((أنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر)). مسلم (٢٢٧٨).

8421 — ‘Abdullah ibn Ja‘far said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “It is not appropriate for a prophet to say: I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (4670), Ahmad (1757), and Abu Ya‘la (6793).
 I say: The statement of the Prophet ﷺ is understood as humility from him. Otherwise, Allah Most High said: “Those messengers — We favored some of them over others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees” [al-Baqarah: 253].
 And the Prophet ﷺ said: “I am the master of the children of Adam, and this is no boast.” Muslim (2278).

arabic_source:
٨٤٢٢ — عن ابن عباس: أن رسول الله ﷺ مر بوادي الأزرق… وفيه: ثم أتى على ثنية هرشى، فقال: ((أي ثنية هذه؟)) قالوا: ثنية هرشى. قال: ((كأني أنظر إلى يونس بن متى عليه السلام على ناقة حمراء جعدة، عليه جبة من صوف، خطام ناقته خلبة، وهو يلبي)). قال هشيم: يعني ليفًا.
 وفي لفظ: “هرشى أو لِفت”، “خطام ناقته ليف خلبة، مارًّا بهذا الوادي ملبيًا”.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٦: ٢٦٨، ٢٦٩).
 قوله: “هرشى”: جبل قريب من الجحفة. وقوله: “جعدة” أي مكتنزة اللحم. وقوله: “خلبة” بضم الخاء وإسكان اللام، وهو الليف. وقوله: “هرشى أو لِفت”: لِفت — بكسر اللام، أو بالفتح، وبفتح اللام والفاء — وهي ثنية بين مكة والمدينة.

8422 — Ibn ‘Abbas narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by Wadi al-Azraq… In it occurs: Then he came upon the pass of Harsha and said: “Which pass is this?” They said: “The pass of Harsha.” He said: “It is as though I can see Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, upon a reddish, compact she-camel, wearing a cloak of wool, the halter of his she-camel made of palm fiber, while he is reciting the talbiyah.” Hushaym said: meaning, fiber.
 In another wording: “Harsha or Lıft,” “the halter of his she-camel was fiber, palm fiber, passing through this valley while reciting the talbiyah.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (166:268, 269).
 His saying “Harsha”: a mountain near al-Juḥfah. His saying “ja‘dah”: compact in flesh. His saying “khulbah,” with ḍammah on the khā’ and sukun on the lām, means palm fiber. His saying “Harsha or Lıft”: Lıft — with kasrah on the lām, or with fatḥah, and with fatḥah on the lām and fā’ — is a pass between Makkah and Medina.

٨٤٢٣ — عن أنس بن مالك أن النبي ﷺ قال: ((موسى بن عمران صفي الله)).
 حسن: رواه الحاكم (٢/٥٧٦) عن عبد الله محمد بن يعقوب الحافظ، حدثنا علي بن الحسن — وهو الهلالي الدرابجردي —، حدثنا أبو ظفر عبد السلام بن مطهر، ثنا جعفر بن سليمان، عن ثابت البناني، عن أنس بن مالك.

 حسن: رواه الحاكم (٢/٥٧٦) عن عبد الله محمد بن يعقوب الحافظ، حدثنا علي بن الحسن — وهو الهلالي الدرابجردي —، حدثنا أبو ظفر عبد السلام بن مطهر، ثنا جعفر بن سليمان، عن ثابت البناني، عن أنس بن مالك.
8423 — Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Musa ibn ‘Imran is the chosen one of Allah.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Hakim (2/576) through ‘Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub al-Hafiz, from ‘Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hilali al-Darabjirdi, from Abu Zafar ‘Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar, from Ja‘far ibn Sulayman, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik.

٨٤٢٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ: ((حين أُسري بي لقيت موسى عليه السلام))، فنعته النبي ﷺ: ((فإذا رجل — حسبته قال: مضطرب — رجل الرأس، كأنه من رجال شنوءة…)) الحديث.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٣٧)، ومسلم (١٦٨: ٢٧٢) — واللفظ له.
 وفي لفظ البخاري (٣٣٩٤): ((رأيت موسى، وإذا رجل ضرب، رجل، كأنه من رجال شنوءة…)).

8424 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Musa, peace be upon him,” and the Prophet ﷺ described him: “He was a man — I think he said: slender — with lank hair, as though he were from the men of Shanu’ah…” the hadith.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3437) and Muslim (168:272) — this is his wording.
 In al-Bukhari’s wording (3394): “I saw Musa, and he was a slender, lank-haired man, as though he were from the men of Shanu’ah…”

٨٤٢٥ — عن ابن عباس قال: ذكر النبي ﷺ ليلة أُسري به، فقال: ((موسى آدم طوال، كأنه من رجال شنوءة)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٩٦)، ومسلم (١٦٥: ٢٦٦).
 وفي لفظ مسلم: ((مررت ليلة أُسري بي على موسى بن عمران عليه السلام، رجل آدم طوال جعد، كأنه من رجال شنوءة…)).
 قوله: “من رجال شنوءة”: بفتح المعجمة وضم النون وسكون الواو، وهي حي من اليمن، ينسبون إلى شنوءة، وهو عبد الله بن كعب بن عبد الله بن مالك بن نصر بن الأزد، ولقب شنوءة لشنآن كان بينه وبين أهله، والنسبة إليه شنوئي.
 قال ابن قتيبة: سمي بذلك من قولك: رجل فيه شنوءة، أي تقزز. والتقزز: التباعد من الأدناس. قال الداودي: رجال الأزد معروفون بالطول. انظر: الفتح (٦/٤٢٩).

english_source:
8425 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned the night he was taken on the Night Journey and said: “Musa was brown-skinned and tall, as though he were from the men of Shanu’ah.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3396) and Muslim (165:266).
 In Muslim’s wording: “On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by Musa ibn ‘Imran, peace be upon him, a brown-skinned, tall, curly-haired man, as though he were from the men of Shanu’ah…”
 His saying “from the men of Shanu’ah”: with fatḥah on the dotted letter, ḍammah on the nūn, and sukun on the wāw. It is a tribe from Yemen, attributed to Shanu’ah, who was ‘Abdullah ibn Ka‘b ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Malik ibn Naṣr ibn al-Azd. He was nicknamed Shanu’ah because of enmity between him and his family, and the attribution to him is Shanū’ī.
 Ibn Qutaybah said: He was named from the saying, “a man with shanū’ah,” meaning aversion. Aversion is distancing oneself from impurities. Al-Dawudi said: The men of al-Azd are known for tallness. See al-Fatḥ (6/429).

٨٤٢٦ — عن عبد الله بن عباس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((… وأما موسى فرجل آدم جعد على جمل أحمر مخطوم بخلبة، كأني أنظر إليه إذا انحدر في الوادي يلبي)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٥٥)، ومسلم (١٦٦: ٢٧٠).

8426 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “…As for Musa, he was a brown-skinned, curly-haired man upon a red camel bridled with palm-fiber. It is as though I can see him as he descends into the valley, reciting the talbiyah.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1555) and Muslim (166:270).

arabic_source:
٨٤٢٧ — عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي ﷺ: ((رأيت عيسى وموسى وإبراهيم. فأما عيسى فأحمر جعد عريض الصدر، وأما موسى فآدم جسيم سبط، كأنه من رجال الزط)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٣٨).
 قوله: “جسيم” أي قوي البدن، ليس بالجسيم ولا بالنحيف البائن، وإنما هو ضرب من الرجال وسط بينهما.
 قوله: “الزط”: طوال غير غلاظ، فليس هو بالنحيف الهزيل، ولا الطويل الفاحش المفرط في الطول. وقيل غير ذلك، وهذا أولى ما قيل في وصفه.

english_source:
8427 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “I saw ‘Isa, Musa, and Ibrahim. As for ‘Isa, he was reddish, curly-haired, and broad-chested. As for Musa, he was brown-skinned, strong-bodied, and straight-haired, as though he were from the men of al-Zuṭṭ.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3438).
 His saying “jasīm” means strong-bodied; not extremely bulky and not clearly thin, but rather a type of man between the two.
 His saying “al-Zuṭṭ”: tall but not bulky. Thus, he was not thin and frail, nor excessively tall beyond proportion. Other explanations have been given, but this is the strongest description.

 قوله: “جسيم” أي قوي البدن، ليس بالجسيم ولا بالنحيف البائن، وإنما هو ضرب من الرجال وسط بينهما.
 قوله: “الزط”: طوال غير غلاظ، فليس هو بالنحيف الهزيل، ولا الطويل الفاحش المفرط في الطول. وقيل غير ذلك، وهذا أولى ما قيل في وصفه.
8427 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “I saw ‘Isa, Musa, and Ibrahim. As for ‘Isa, he was reddish, curly-haired, and broad-chested. As for Musa, he was brown-skinned, strong-bodied, and straight-haired, as though he were from the men of al-Zuṭṭ.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3438).
 His saying “jasīm” means strong-bodied; not extremely bulky and not clearly thin, but rather a type of man between the two.
 His saying “al-Zuṭṭ”: tall but not bulky. Thus, he was not thin and frail, nor excessively tall beyond proportion. Other explanations have been given, but this is the strongest description.

٨٤٢٨ — عن ابن عباس قال: سرنا مع رسول الله ﷺ بين مكة والمدينة، فمررنا بواد، فقال: ((أي واد هذا؟)) فقالوا: وادي الأزرق. فقال: ((كأني أنظر إلى موسى ﷺ))، فذكر من لونه وشعره شيئًا لم يحفظه داود، ((واضعًا إصبعيه في أذنيه، له جؤار إلى الله بالتلبية، مارًّا بهذا الوادي…)).
 وفي لفظ: ((كأني أنظر إلى موسى عليه السلام هابطًا من الثنية، وله جؤار إلى الله بالتلبية)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٦: ٢٦٨، ٢٦٩).

8428 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: We traveled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between Makkah and Medina, and we passed by a valley. He said: “Which valley is this?” They said: “Wadi al-Azraq.” He said: “It is as though I can see Musa ﷺ,” and he mentioned something of his color and hair that Dawud did not memorize, “placing his two fingers in his ears, raising his voice to Allah with the talbiyah, passing through this valley…”
 In another wording: “It is as though I can see Musa, peace be upon him, descending from the pass, raising his voice to Allah with the talbiyah.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (166:268, 269).

 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٧: ٢٧١).

٨٤٣٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((كانت بنو إسرائيل يغتسلون عراة، ينظر بعضهم إلى سوأة بعض، وكان موسى عليه السلام يغتسل وحده. فقالوا: والله ما يمنع موسى أن يغتسل معنا إلا أنه آدر. قال: فذهب مرة يغتسل، فوضع ثوبه على حجر، ففر الحجر بثوبه. قال: فجمع موسى بإثره يقول: ثوبي حجر، ثوبي حجر، حتى نظرت بنو إسرائيل إلى سوأة موسى. قالوا: والله ما بموسى من بأس. فقام الحجر حتى نُظر إليه. قال: فأخذ ثوبه، فطفق بالحجر ضربًا)). قال أبو هريرة: والله إنه بالحجر ندب، ستة أو سبعة، ضرب موسى بالحجر.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٧٨)، ومسلم (٣٣٩: ١٥٥).

8430 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, some of them looking at the nakedness of others, while Musa, peace be upon him, used to bathe alone. They said: By Allah, nothing prevents Musa from bathing with us except that he has swollen testicles. He said: One time he went to bathe and placed his garment on a stone, and the stone ran away with his garment. He said: Musa went after it, saying: My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone! until the Children of Israel looked at Musa’s body. They said: By Allah, there is nothing wrong with Musa. Then the stone stopped where it could be seen. He took his garment and began striking the stone.” Abu Hurayrah said: By Allah, there are marks on the stone — six or seven — from Musa striking the stone.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (278) and Muslim (339:155).

٨٤٣١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن موسى كان رجلًا حييًّا ستيرًا، لا يُرى من جلده شيء استحياءً منه، فآذاه من آذاه من بني إسرائيل، فقالوا: ما يستتر هذا التستر إلا من عيب بجلده: إما برص، وإما أُدرة، وإما آفة. وإن الله أراد أن يبرئه مما قالوا لموسى، فخلا يومًا وحده، فوضع ثيابه على الحجر، ثم اغتسل. فلما فرغ أقبل إلى ثيابه ليأخذها، وإن الحجر عدا بثوبه، فأخذ موسى عصاه، وطلب الحجر، فجعل يقول: ثوبي حجر، ثوبي حجر، حتى انتهى إلى ملإ من بني إسرائيل، فرأوه عريانًا أحسن ما خلق الله، وأبرأه مما يقولون. وقام الحجر، فأخذ ثوبه فلبسه، وطفق بالحجر ضربًا بعصاه، فوالله إن بالحجر لندبًا من أثر ضربه، ثلاثًا أو أربعًا أو خمسًا. فذلك قوله: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا، لَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ آذَوْا مُوسَىٰ، فَبَرَّأَهُ اللهُ مِمَّا قَالُوا، وَكَانَ عِندَ اللهِ وَجِيهًا))).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٠٤).
 وقوله: “لندبًا” أي أثرًا.

8431 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Musa was a very modest and covered man; nothing of his skin was seen because of his modesty. Some of the Children of Israel harmed him, saying: He only covers himself so much because of a defect in his skin — either leprosy, swollen testicles, or some other affliction. Allah wanted to clear him of what they said about Musa. So one day he was alone, placed his clothes on a stone, and bathed. When he finished, he came to his clothes to take them, but the stone had run away with his garment. Musa took his staff and pursued the stone, saying: My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone! until he reached a gathering of the Children of Israel. They saw him naked, in the best form Allah had created, and Allah cleared him of what they had been saying. The stone stopped, so he took his garment and put it on, then began striking the stone with his staff. By Allah, there were marks on the stone from his striking it — three, four, or five. That is His saying: ‘O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa; then Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.’”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3404).
 His saying “marks” means traces.

٨٤٣١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن موسى كان رجلًا حييًّا ستيرًا، لا يُرى من جلده شيء استحياءً منه، فآذاه من آذاه من بني إسرائيل، فقالوا: ما يستتر هذا التستر إلا من عيب بجلده: إما برص، وإما أُدرة، وإما آفة. وإن الله أراد أن يبرئه مما قالوا لموسى، فخلا يومًا وحده، فوضع ثيابه على الحجر، ثم اغتسل. فلما فرغ أقبل إلى ثيابه ليأخذها، وإن الحجر عدا بثوبه، فأخذ موسى عصاه، وطلب الحجر، فجعل يقول: ثوبي حجر، ثوبي حجر، حتى انتهى إلى ملإ من بني إسرائيل، فرأوه عريانًا أحسن ما خلق الله، وأبرأه مما يقولون. وقام الحجر، فأخذ ثوبه فلبسه، وطفق بالحجر ضربًا بعصاه، فوالله إن بالحجر لندبًا من أثر ضربه، ثلاثًا أو أربعًا أو خمسًا. فذلك قوله: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا، لَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ آذَوْا مُوسَىٰ، فَبَرَّأَهُ اللهُ مِمَّا قَالُوا، وَكَانَ عِندَ اللهِ وَجِيهًا))).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٠٤).
 وقوله: “لندبًا” أي أثرًا.
8431 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Musa was a very modest and covered man; nothing of his skin was seen because of his modesty. Some of the Children of Israel harmed him, saying: He only covers himself so much because of a defect in his skin — either leprosy, swollen testicles, or some other affliction. Allah wanted to clear him of what they said about Musa. So one day he was alone, placed his clothes on a stone, and bathed. When he finished, he came to his clothes to take them, but the stone had run away with his garment. Musa took his staff and pursued the stone, saying: My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone! until he reached a gathering of the Children of Israel. They saw him naked, in the best form Allah had created, and Allah cleared him of what they had been saying. The stone stopped, so he took his garment and put it on, then began striking the stone with his staff. By Allah, there were marks on the stone from his striking it — three, four, or five. That is His saying: ‘O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa; then Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.’”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3404).
 His saying “marks” means traces.

8432 — Abu Hurayrah said: Musa, peace be upon him, was a very modest man. He said: He would not be seen uncovered. The Children of Israel said: “He has swollen testicles.” He said: He bathed near a water-place and placed his garment on a stone. The stone ran away, and he followed it with his staff, striking it and saying: “My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone!” until it stopped before a gathering of the Children of Israel. Then this was revealed:
 “O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa; then Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (339:156).
 His saying “ādar” means one with enlarged testicles.

٨٤٣٣ — عن سعيد بن جبير قال: سألني يهودي من أهل الحيرة: أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟ قلت: لا أدري حتى أقدم على حبر العرب فأسأله. فقدمت، فسألت ابن عباس، فقال: قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما، إن رسول الله ﷺ إذا قال فعل.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٨٤).

8433 — Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: A Jew from the people of al-Ḥirah asked me: “Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?” I said: “I do not know until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him.” So I came and asked Ibn ‘Abbas, and he said: “He fulfilled the longer and better of the two. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says something, he does it.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2684).

٨٤٣٥ — عن عائشة قالت: كان أول ما بُدئ به رسول الله ﷺ من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم. وفيه: فرجع النبي ﷺ إلى خديجة يرجف فؤاده، فانطلقت به إلى ورقة بن نوفل، وكان رجلًا تنصر، يقرأ الإنجيل بالعربية. فقال ورقة: ماذا ترى؟ فأخبره، فقال ورقة: هذا الناموس الذي أنزل الله على موسى، وإن أدركني يومك أنصرك نصرًا مؤزرًا.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٩٢)، ومسلم (١٦٠: ٢٥٢).

8435 — ‘A’ishah said: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began of revelation was true dreams in sleep. In it occurs: The Prophet ﷺ returned to Khadijah with his heart trembling, so she took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal. He was a man who had become Christian and used to read the Gospel in Arabic. Waraqah said: “What do you see?” He informed him, and Waraqah said: “This is the Namus that Allah sent down upon Musa. If I live to see your day, I will support you with strong support.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3392) and Muslim (160:252).

8435 — ‘A’ishah said: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began of revelation was true dreams in sleep. In it occurs: The Prophet ﷺ returned to Khadijah with his heart trembling, so she took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal. He was a man who had become Christian and used to read the Gospel in Arabic. Waraqah said: “What do you see?” He informed him, and Waraqah said: “This is the Namus that Allah sent down upon Musa. If I live to see your day, I will support you with strong support.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3392) and Muslim (160:252).

arabic_source:
٨٤٣٦ — عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ لما قدم المدينة وجدهم يصومون يومًا — يعني عاشوراء — فقالوا: هذا يوم عظيم، وهو يوم نجّى الله فيه موسى، وأغرق آل فرعون، فصام موسى شكرًا لله. فقال: ((أنا أولى بموسى منهم)) فصامه وأمر بصيامه.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٩٧)، ومسلم (١١٣٠: ١٢٧). وهذا لفظ البخاري.
 وفي لفظ مسلم: هذا اليوم الذي أظهر الله فيه موسى وبني إسرائيل على فرعون، فنحن نصومه تعظيمًا له. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((نحن أحق بموسى منكم))، فأمر بصومه.

english_source:
8436 — Ibn ‘Abbas narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, he found them fasting a day — meaning ‘Ashura’. They said: “This is a great day. It is the day on which Allah saved Musa and drowned the people of Pharaoh, so Musa fasted it out of gratitude to Allah.” He said: “I have more right to Musa than they do.” So he fasted it and commanded that it be fasted.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3397) and Muslim (1130:127). This is al-Bukhari’s wording.
 In Muslim’s wording: “This is the day on which Allah gave Musa and the Children of Israel victory over Pharaoh, so we fast it in veneration of it.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “We have more right to Musa than you do,” and he commanded that it be fasted.

٨٤٣٧ — عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((الناس يُصعقون يوم القيامة، فأكون أول من يفيق، فإذا أنا بموسى آخذ بقائمة من قوائم العرش، فلا أدري أفاق قبلي، أم جوزي بصعقة الطور)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٩٨)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٤: ١٦٢).

8437 — Abu Sa‘id narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “The people will fall unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness. Then I will see Musa holding onto one of the legs of the Throne. I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or whether he was recompensed for the shock at the Mount.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3398) and Muslim (2374:162).

arabic_source:
٨٤٣٨ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((لا تخيروني على موسى، فإن الناس يصعقون يوم القيامة، فأصعق معهم، فأكون أول من يفيق، فإذا موسى باطش جانب العرش، فلا أدري أكان فيمن صعق فأفاق قبلي، أو كان ممن استثنى الله)). والحديث فيه قصة.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤١١)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٣: ١٥٩).

8438 — Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Do not give me preference over Musa, for the people will fall unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will fall unconscious with them. Then I will be the first to regain consciousness, and Musa will be grasping the side of the Throne. I do not know whether he was among those who fell unconscious and regained consciousness before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah exempted.” The hadith contains a story.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2411) and Muslim (2373:159).

٨٤٣٩ — عن أنس، أن النبي ﷺ قرأ هذه الآية: (فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ، جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا) [الأعراف: ١٤٣]. قال حماد: هكذا، وأمسك سليمان بطرف إبهامه على أنملة أصبعه اليمنى. قال: فساخ الجبل: (وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقًا).
 صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٠٧٤)، وأحمد (١٢٢٦٠)، وابن أبي عاصم في السنة (٤٨٠، ٤٨١)، والحاكم (٢/٣٢٠).

8439 — Anas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse: “So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble” [al-A‘raf: 143]. Ḥammad said: “Like this,” and Sulayman held the tip of his thumb against the joint of his right finger. He said: Then the mountain sank down: “And Musa fell unconscious.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3074), Ahmad (12260), Ibn Abi ‘Aṣim in al-Sunnah (480, 481), and al-Hakim (2/320).

٨٤٤٠ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: لما كان يوم حنين آثر رسول الله ﷺ ناسًا في القسمة، فأعطى الأقرع بن حابس مائة من الإبل، وأعطى عيينة مثل ذلك، وأعطى ناسًا من أشراف العرب، وآثرهم يومئذ في القسمة. فقال رجل: والله إن هذه لقسمة ما عُدل فيها، وما أُريد فيها وجه الله. قال: فقلت: والله لأخبرن رسول الله ﷺ. قال: فأتيته فأخبرته بما قال. قال: فتغير وجهه حتى كان كالصرف، ثم قال: ((فمن يعدل إن لم يعدل الله ورسوله؟)) قال: ثم قال: ((يرحم الله موسى، قد أوذي بأكثر من هذا فصبر)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٥٠)، ومسلم (١٠٦٢: ١٤٠).

8440 — ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud said: On the day of Ḥunayn, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ favored some people in the distribution. He gave al-Aqra‘ ibn Ḥabis one hundred camels, gave ‘Uyaynah the same, and gave some nobles of the Arabs, favoring them that day in the distribution. A man said: “By Allah, this is a distribution in which justice has not been done, and by which the Face of Allah was not intended.” He said: I said: “By Allah, I will inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: I came to him and informed him of what he had said. His face changed until it became like red dye, then he said: “Who will be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just?” Then he said: “May Allah have mercy on Musa. He was harmed with more than this, yet he was patient.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3150) and Muslim (1062:140).

٨٤٤٠ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: لما كان يوم حنين آثر رسول الله ﷺ ناسًا في القسمة، فأعطى الأقرع بن حابس مائة من الإبل، وأعطى عيينة مثل ذلك، وأعطى ناسًا من أشراف العرب، وآثرهم يومئذ في القسمة. فقال رجل: والله إن هذه لقسمة ما عُدل فيها، وما أُريد فيها وجه الله. قال: فقلت: والله لأخبرن رسول الله ﷺ. قال: فأتيته فأخبرته بما قال. قال: فتغير وجهه حتى كان كالصرف، ثم قال: ((فمن يعدل إن لم يعدل الله ورسوله؟)) قال: ثم قال: ((يرحم الله موسى، قد أوذي بأكثر من هذا فصبر)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٥٠)، ومسلم (١٠٦٢: ١٤٠).

٨٤٤١ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة مرفوعًا: ((سأل موسى ربه: ما أدنى أهل الجنة منزلة؟ قال: هو رجل يجيء بعدما أُدخل أهل الجنة الجنة، فيقال له: ادخل الجنة. فيقول: أي رب، كيف وقد نزل الناس منازلهم وأخذوا أخذاتهم؟ فيقال له: أترضى أن يكون لك مثل ملك ملك من ملوك الدنيا؟ فيقول: رضيت رب. فيقول: لك ذلك ومثله ومثله ومثله ومثله. فقال في الخامسة: رضيت رب. فيقول: لك ذلك وعشرة أمثاله، ولك ما اشتهت نفسك ولذت عينك. فيقول: رضيت رب. قال: رب، فأعلاهم منزلة؟ قال: أولئك الذين أردت، غرست كرامتهم بيدي، وختمت عليها، فلم تر عين، ولم تسمع أذن، ولم يخطر على قلب بشر. قال: ومصداقه في كتاب الله عز وجل: (فَلَا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَّا أُخْفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ) الآية)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٩: ٣١٢).

8441 — Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah narrated in marfu‘ form: “Musa asked his Lord: What is the lowest rank of the people of Paradise? He said: It is a man who will come after the people of Paradise have been admitted into Paradise. It will be said to him: Enter Paradise. He will say: My Lord, how, when the people have already taken their places and received their shares? It will be said to him: Would you be pleased to have the like of the kingdom of one of the kings of the world? He will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He will say: You will have that, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it, and the like of it. On the fifth, he will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He will say: You will have that and ten times its like, and you will have whatever your soul desires and whatever delights your eye. He will say: I am pleased, my Lord. He said: My Lord, then what of the highest in rank? He said: They are those whom I intended; I planted their honor with My hand and sealed it, so no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of any human. He said: Its confirmation is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes’ — the verse.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (189:312).

٨٤٤٢ — عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله ﷺ أنه قال: ((سأل موسى ربه عن ست خصال، كان يظن أنها له خالصة، والسابعة لم يكن موسى يحبها. قال: يا رب، أي عبادك أتقى؟ قال: الذي يذكر ولا ينسى. قال: فأي عبادك أهدى؟ قال: الذي يتبع الهدى. قال: فأي عبادك أحكم؟ قال: الذي يحكم للناس كما يحكم لنفسه. قال: فأي عبادك أعلم؟ قال: عالم لا يشبع من العلم، يجمع علم الناس إلى علمه. قال: فأي عبادك أعز؟ قال: الذي إذا قدر غفر. قال: فأي عبادك أغنى؟ قال: الذي يرضى بما يؤتى. قال: فأي عبادك أفقر؟ قال: صاحب منقوص)). قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ليس الغنى عن ظهر، إنما الغنى غنى النفس. وإذا أراد الله بعبد خيرًا جعل غناه في نفسه، وتقاه في قلبه. وإذا أراد الله بعبد شرًّا جعل فقره بين عينيه)).
 حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٦٢١٧).

8442 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Musa asked his Lord about six qualities, thinking that they were exclusively for him, and the seventh was something Musa did not love. He said: My Lord, which of Your servants is most God-fearing? He said: The one who remembers and does not forget. He said: Which of Your servants is most guided? He said: The one who follows guidance. He said: Which of Your servants is most wise in judgment? He said: The one who judges for people as he judges for himself. He said: Which of Your servants is most knowledgeable? He said: A scholar who is never satisfied with knowledge, adding the knowledge of people to his own knowledge. He said: Which of Your servants is most honorable? He said: The one who, when he has power, forgives. He said: Which of Your servants is richest? He said: The one who is content with what he is given. He said: Which of Your servants is poorest? He said: The one who always feels deprived.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Richness is not from outward possessions; richness is the richness of the soul. When Allah intends good for a servant, He places his richness in his soul and his piety in his heart. When Allah intends evil for a servant, He places his poverty before his eyes.”
 Good: Narrated by Ibn Hibban (6217).

٨٤٤٢ — عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله ﷺ أنه قال: ((سأل موسى ربه عن ست خصال، كان يظن أنها له خالصة، والسابعة لم يكن موسى يحبها. قال: يا رب، أي عبادك أتقى؟ قال: الذي يذكر ولا ينسى. قال: فأي عبادك أهدى؟ قال: الذي يتبع الهدى. قال: فأي عبادك أحكم؟ قال: الذي يحكم للناس كما يحكم لنفسه. قال: فأي عبادك أعلم؟ قال: عالم لا يشبع من العلم، يجمع علم الناس إلى علمه. قال: فأي عبادك أعز؟ قال: الذي إذا قدر غفر. قال: فأي عبادك أغنى؟ قال: الذي يرضى بما يؤتى. قال: فأي عبادك أفقر؟ قال: صاحب منقوص)). قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ليس الغنى عن ظهر، إنما الغنى غنى النفس. وإذا أراد الله بعبد خيرًا جعل غناه في نفسه، وتقاه في قلبه. وإذا أراد الله بعبد شرًّا جعل فقره بين عينيه)).
 حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٦٢١٧).
8442 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Musa asked his Lord about six qualities, thinking that they were exclusively for him, and the seventh was something Musa did not love. He said: My Lord, which of Your servants is most God-fearing? He said: The one who remembers and does not forget. He said: Which of Your servants is most guided? He said: The one who follows guidance. He said: Which of Your servants is most wise in judgment? He said: The one who judges for people as he judges for himself. He said: Which of Your servants is most knowledgeable? He said: A scholar who is never satisfied with knowledge, adding the knowledge of people to his own knowledge. He said: Which of Your servants is most honorable? He said: The one who, when he has power, forgives. He said: Which of Your servants is richest? He said: The one who is content with what he is given. He said: Which of Your servants is poorest? He said: The one who always feels deprived.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Richness is not from outward possessions; richness is the richness of the soul. When Allah intends good for a servant, He places his richness in his soul and his piety in his heart. When Allah intends evil for a servant, He places his poverty before his eyes.”
 Good: Narrated by Ibn Hibban (6217).

٨٤٤٤ — عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله ﷺ: ((جاء ملك الموت إلى موسى عليه السلام، فقال له: أجب ربك. قال: فلطم موسى عليه السلام عين ملك الموت ففقأها. قال: فرجع الملك إلى الله تعالى، قال: إنك أرسلتني إلى عبد لك لا يريد الموت، وقد فقأ عيني. قال: فرد الله إليه عينه، وقال: ارجع إلى عبدي فقل: الحياة تريد؟ فإن كنت تريد الحياة، فضع يدك على متن ثور، فما توارت يدك من شعرة فإنك تعيش بها سنة. قال: ثم مه؟ قال: ثم تموت. قال: فالآن من قريب، رب أمتني من الأرض المقدسة رمية بحجر)). قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((والله لو أني عنده لأريتكم قبره إلى جانب الطريق عند الكثيب الأحمر)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٣٧٣).
 في الحديث أن موسى عليه السلام لطم ملك الموت ففقأ عينه، وذلك لأنه دخل داره بغير إذنه، ولم يعرفه أنه ملك الموت، وقال له: أجب ربك، فلطمه لدخوله بيته بغير استئذان. فلما تبين له أنه ملك الموت، وخُيّر بين الحياة والموت، اختار الموت.

8444 — Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “The Angel of Death came to Musa, peace be upon him, and said to him: Respond to your Lord. He said: Musa, peace be upon him, struck the eye of the Angel of Death and knocked it out. The angel returned to Allah Most High and said: You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want death, and he knocked out my eye. He said: Allah restored his eye to him and said: Return to My servant and say: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand on the back of an ox, and for every hair your hand covers, you will live a year. He said: Then what? He said: Then you will die. He said: Then now, soon. My Lord, cause me to die at the distance of a stone’s throw from the Holy Land.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “By Allah, if I were there, I would show you his grave beside the road near the red sandhill.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2373).
 In the hadith, Musa, peace be upon him, struck the Angel of Death and knocked out his eye. This was because he entered his house without permission, and Musa did not know that he was the Angel of Death. He said to him: “Respond to your Lord,” so Musa struck him because he had entered his house without seeking permission. When it became clear to him that he was the Angel of Death, and he was given the choice between life and death, he chose death.

8445 — Anas narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I came upon Musa, peace be upon him, on the night I was taken on the Night Journey, near the red sandhill, and he was standing, praying in his grave.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2375:165).
 His saying, “and he was standing, praying in his grave,” is understood as referring to the life of the Barzakh, not worldly life.

٨٤٤٦ — عن مالك بن صعصعة قال: قال النبي ﷺ: ((بينا أنا عند البيت بين النائم واليقظان…)) في قصة الإسراء، وفيه: ((فأتينا على السماء السادسة، قيل: من هذا؟ قيل: جبريل. قيل: من معك؟ قيل: محمد. قيل: وقد أرسل إليه؟ مرحبًا به، ولنعم المجيء جاء. فأتيت على موسى، فسلمت عليه، فقال: مرحبًا بك من أخ ونبي. فلما جاوزت بكى، فقيل: ما أبكاك؟ قال: يا رب، هذا الغلام الذي بعث بعدي يدخل الجنة من أمته أكثر مما يدخل من أمتي…)).

8446 — Malik ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “While I was at the House, between sleep and wakefulness…” in the story of the Isra’. In it occurs: “Then we came to the sixth heaven. Then I came upon Musa, greeted him with salām, and he said: Welcome to you as a brother and a prophet. When I passed him, he wept. It was said: What has made you weep? He said: My Lord, this young man who was sent after me will have more of his Ummah enter Paradise than will enter from my Ummah…”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3207) and Muslim (164:264).

٨٤٤٧ — عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((أُتيت بالبراق…)) في قصة الإسراء والمعراج، وفيه: ((ثم عرج بنا إلى السماء السادسة، فاستفتح جبريل عليه السلام. قيل: من هذا؟ قال: جبريل. قيل: ومن معك؟ قال: محمد. قيل: وقد بعث إليه؟ قال: قد بعث إليه. ففتح لنا، فإذا أنا بموسى، فرحب ودعا لي بخير)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٢: ٢٥٩).

8447 — Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was brought al-Buraq…” in the story of the Isra’ and Mi‘raj. In it occurs: “Then we were taken up to the sixth heaven, and Jibril, peace be upon him, asked for it to be opened. It was said: Who is this? He said: Jibril. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent for? He said: He has been sent for. So it was opened for us, and there I was with Musa. He welcomed me and supplicated for good for me.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (162:259).

٨٤٤٨ — عن حصين بن عبد الرحمن قال: كنت عند سعيد بن جبير، فقال: أيكم رأى الكوكب الذي انقض البارحة؟ قلت: أنا. ثم قلت: أما إني لم أكن في صلاة، ولكني لُدغت. قال: فماذا صنعت؟ قلت: استرقيت. قال: فما حملك على ذلك؟ قلت: حديث حدثناه الشعبي. فقال: وما حدثكم الشعبي؟ قلت: حدثنا عن بريدة بن الحصيب الأسلمي أنه قال: لا رقية إلا من عين أو حُمَة. فقال: قد أحسن من انتهى إلى ما سمع.
 ولكن حدثنا ابن عباس، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((عُرضت علي الأمم، فرأيت النبي ومعه الرهط، والنبي ومعه الرجل والرجلان، والنبي ليس معه أحد، إذ رُفع لي سواد عظيم، فظننت أنهم أمتي، فقيل لي: هذا موسى ﷺ وقومه، ولكن انظر إلى الأفق. فنظرت، فإذا سواد عظيم. فقيل لي: انظر إلى الأفق الآخر، فإذا سواد عظيم. فقيل لي: هذه أمتك، ومعهم سبعون ألفًا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا عذاب)). ثم نهض، فدخل منزله، فخاض الناس في أولئك الذين يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا عذاب، فقال بعضهم: فلعلهم الذين صحبوا رسول الله ﷺ، وقال بعضهم: فلعلهم الذين وُلدوا في الإسلام ولم يشركوا بالله، وذكروا أشياء. فخرج عليهم رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: ((ما الذي تخوضون فيه؟)) فأخبروه، فقال: ((هم الذين لا يرقون ولا يسترقون ولا يتطيرون، وعلى ربهم يتوكلون)). فقام عكاشة بن محصن، فقال: ادع الله أن يجعلني منهم. فقال: ((أنت منهم)). ثم قام رجل آخر، فقال: ادع الله أن يجعلني منهم. فقال: ((سبقك بها عكاشة)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٥٤١)، ومسلم (٢٢٠: ٣٧٤، ٣٧٥).

8448 — Ḥuṣayn ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥman said: I was with Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and he said: “Which of you saw the star that fell last night?” I said: “I did.” Then I said: “But I was not in prayer; rather, I had been stung.” He said: “What did you do?” I said: “I sought ruqyah.” He said: “What led you to do that?” I said: “A hadith that al-Sha‘bi narrated to us.” He said: “And what did al-Sha‘bi narrate to you?” I said: “He narrated to us from Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb al-Aslami that he said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a venomous sting.” He said: “The one who acts according to what he has heard has done well.
 But Ibn ‘Abbas narrated to us from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: ‘The nations were shown to me. I saw a prophet with a small group, a prophet with one or two men, and a prophet with no one with him. Then a great dark mass was raised before me, and I thought they were my Ummah. It was said to me: This is Musa ﷺ and his people, but look toward the horizon. I looked, and there was a great dark mass. It was said to me: Look toward the other horizon. There was another great dark mass. It was said to me: This is your Ummah, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment.’” Then he rose and entered his house. The people began discussing those who would enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment. Some said: “Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Others said: “Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and never associated anything with Allah.” They mentioned other things. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them and said: “What are you discussing?” They informed him, and he said: “They are those who do not perform ruqyah, do not seek ruqyah, do not believe in omens, and place their trust in their Lord.” ‘Ukashah ibn Miḥṣan stood and said: “Supplicate to Allah to make me one of them.” He said: “You are one of them.” Then another man stood and said: “Supplicate to Allah to make me one of them.” He said: “‘Ukashah has preceded you in it.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6541) and Muslim (220:374, 375).
